review_oracle: Independent QC Manager: deterministic declared-observation evaluation plus mandatory external media/image proof and distinct human reviewer; this is NOT automatic vision recognition

shots.artistic_question: Does care take physical form in the exchange of food and light, rather than anonymous luminous spectacle?
shots.primary_action: Two fictional market customers visibly transfer one bowl hand-to-hand; the receiver accepts it while the vendor remains involved with everyday maintenance.
scene_graph: ONE intimate Taiwan-style night-market aisle at human eye height
single vendor and two identifiable-as-separate fictional customers in the middle ground
one bowl crossing the interpersonal gap with hands in contact
wet steel directly reflecting one visible practical tungsten bulb; no external magic light
surrounding people remain context, not the hero subject
shots.camera: 24 mm, human height, frame prioritizes the bowl exchange; preserve negative space for real human distance
shots.time_logic: Video: bowl changes hands between t=1.2 and t=2.4 s. Warm specular contour at t=3.3–4.0 s can match S03, with independently plausible local source.
negative_constraints: No postcard-wide crowd as sole subject
No hanging-light canopy used as substitute for the bowl exchange
No invented rainbow without matching physical light/source

checks.criterion: Both hands and one visibly transferring bowl appear in the usable shot frame
A physically visible local lamp is associated with a reflection on wet steel
The crowd and overhead string lamps replace the required interpersonal exchange
Second camera angle/paired S03 comparison documents a comparable contour without shared impossible light

references: Rirkrit Tiravanija, untitled 1990 (pad thai): participation, not copying the event
Olafur Eliasson, Beauty: observer-angle and local light/material logic only

shots.artistic_question: Can an unformed wire object be perceived as living only after a gradual change in viewpoint or focus?
shots.primary_action: A tiny original irregular wire-and-filament object beside a CLOSED worn child's suitcase evolves from ambiguous metal segments into a fleeting recognisable bird-like gestalt.
scene_graph: closed small suitcase with unmarked worn surface
single weak incandescent filament, thin asymmetrical metal wire structure
three consistent construction joints, no ornamental feathers or complete sculpted wings in the first read
lamp source remains physically local and subdued
shots.camera: 85 mm tactile macro, sparse optical field, weak filament against subdued shadow
shots.time_logic: Initial frame must leave silhouette ambiguous; only focal shift or gentle rotation later allows the same physical wire to read as a bird. Preserve three identical joints for S24.
negative_constraints: No fully finished gilded bird sculpture
No ornamental filigree wings, company-bird logo or golden mascot
No levitation or magic sparkle showing the answer from first frame

checks.criterion: At the beginning the subject visibly reads as irregular assembled wire, not a completed bird statue
Three repeatable asymmetric metal junctions are observable in the geometry
A polished or gilded bird silhouette is already unmistakable in the initial still
Video establishes a later viewpoint/focus change that completes the bird reading without adding new geometry
S24 bird compares to the same three physical joints and wire proportions

references: Studio DRIFT, Fragile Future III: fragile handmade electronic material (no copied design)
Jim Campbell, Tilted Plane: incomplete/low-resolution perceptual recognition (no LED array copy)

shots.artistic_question: Can the same physical scene change which lighting system seems valuable without a simplistic illustrative split?
shots.primary_action: A hand transfers a repairable warm paper-covered live lamp at a communal workbench; behind thick glass, a BRIGHTER SEALED TECHNICAL lighting assembly stands inaccessible.
scene_graph: ONE continuous workshop and shared floor plane with foreground bench and deep background glass barrier
visible active exchange of a small patched paper lamp module between distinct people
sealed modern technical light with cooling condensation behind glass
background technical system does not take the form of an antique lantern or nostalgic streetlight
shots.camera: 35 mm deep composition; begin foreground action, use soft focus redistribution instead of picture split
shots.time_logic: Video: one focus/attention shift moves from human-scale repair to sealed remote system without spatial cut.
negative_constraints: No split-screen, collage, diptych, two-panel composition or abrupt architectural discontinuity
No old street lantern as stand-in for sealed compute system
No giant lantern market as a substitute for the collaborative workbench

checks.criterion: Foreground shared workbench and sealed background device coexist in ONE continuous physical composition
A small repairable lamp is visibly being passed between human hands
Behind glass is a brighter sealed technical light source with believable cooling apparatus
The result is a side-by-side split image, diptych or unconnected street scenes
Video uses a single contiguous scene to shift focus between two systems

references: Felix Gonzalez-Torres, Untitled (Placebo): take/renew/participation (no candy pile)
Dan Graham, Two-way Mirror Cylinder inside Cube and a Video Salon: distributed viewing not copied structure

shots.artistic_question: Can a barely-noticed, handmade paper object retrospectively reframe a monumental automated factory?
shots.primary_action: Show an orderly, functioning fictional electronics line where vacant BLUE stools retain folded work gloves and ONE unfinished small paper house with a distinctive offset roof fold and irregular window.
scene_graph: 24 mm low human-height perspective; credible machine line without propaganda lighting
multiple empty blue stools, hand-folded cotton gloves
small visibly HAND-FOLDED unfinished paper house ON one specific stool with offset roof crease and non-rectangular window
house must be sufficiently legible on second viewing without theatrical central spotlight
shots.camera: calm low architectural frame, preserve scale contrast between machinery and human paperwork
shots.time_logic: Initial glance may emphasize empty machines and stools; later S22 reveals the same FOLDING GRAMMAR, not the same physical house.
negative_constraints: No red dystopian factory horror lighting as the only storytelling mechanism
No generic folded tissue/paper scrap substituted for the paper HOUSE

checks.criterion: Visible multiple empty blue stools along the production line
At least one stool shows recognizable folded work gloves
An identifiable small unfinished paper house is visibly on a stool
Offset roof fold and irregular window can be examined for later comparison
The factory is shown without any identifiable miniature paper house
S22 shares roof/window folding grammar without being the same physical paper object

references: Cao Fei, Whose Utopia: worker aspirations outside production quotas (no film recreation)
Liliana Porter, Untitled (with Cube - tall): scale/attention re-reading (no photo-cube copying)

shots.artistic_question: Can precision technology and a damaged acoustic instrument communicate the loss of function using physical evidence rather than beach-disaster symbolism?
shots.primary_action: Inside a COASTAL PRECISION-ENGINEERING LAB, a fictional technician presses an aged salt-swollen upright piano key while a held silicon wafer reflects across the keys.
scene_graph: upright piano INSIDE enclosed precision lab, structurally intact but with localized salt-swollen lower wood
cleanroom technical bench and inactive optical inspection rig adjacent to piano
fictional technician holds thin semiconductor wafer, not colorful plastic CD
one physically traceable reflected arc connects wafer and keys
sea is seen outside through high windows only
shots.camera: 35 mm fixed; simultaneous visibility of pressing finger, aged key and wafer light geometry
shots.time_logic: Video: keypress emits original damp mechanism click with no intact musical attack; reflected wafer contour momentarily resembles notation.
negative_constraints: No upright piano standing on sand or in surf
No scenic white-clothed man holding an oversized rainbow disc as centerpiece
No explicit tsunami aftermath, collapsed city or copied historical instrument

checks.criterion: Piano and technician are inside an enclosed engineering/inspection laboratory
Piano lower wood shows restrained plausible salt wear rather than total ruin
One visible hand presses a real piano key
A plausible small semiconductor wafer is held near the keys with a reflected contour
The piano is standing directly on an outdoor beach/sand shoreline
Video/audio preserves the mechanical key-contact sound without a conventional note

references: Sakamoto and Takatani, IS YOUR TIME: nature alters an instrument's physical time (no physical replica or sampling)
Rebecca Horn, Concert for Anarchy: role inversion, no hanging piano

shots.artistic_question: Who is performing if no one is on stage, but the assembled audience still applauds?
shots.primary_action: Camera ON an empty fictional opera stage looking OUTWARD toward an occupied auditorium; several visible seated audience members applaud while the stage retains a single unoccupied music stand.
scene_graph: Viewpoint from the stage facing auditorium and boxes (not an audience-seat view toward a display coat)
human audience visibly seated and some hands visibly applauding
empty stage has an unoccupied music stand
asymmetric tarnished reflector catches fragmented audience silhouettes, making watchers the seen subject
some audience seats may be empty; the whole auditorium must NOT be unoccupied
shots.camera: 35 mm fixed from stage; spectators legible in depth, stage absence obvious
shots.time_logic: Video: audible spatial handclaps arise from present humans; reflection redirects attention to their own image. No performance takes place.
negative_constraints: No ornate royal robe displayed as central hero object
No empty auditorium with no humans to clap
No visible singer, performer, musician, or central stage costume

checks.criterion: An identifiable audience including multiple seated human observers is clearly visible
More than one visibly present spectator is actually applauding
The stage has no performer, leaving an unoccupied stand as evidence
A physical reflector returns audience silhouettes toward their own position
A gold robe or other elaborate costume occupies the primary theatrical focus
All spectator seats are empty, making the required applauding audience impossible
Original spatial applause source tracks present spectators and room reverberation

references: Janet Cardiff and George Bures Miller, The Murder of Crows: spatial sound narrative only (no recordings)
Dan Graham, Performer/Audience/Mirror: audience becomes performer (no performance replay)
